messages:
Maya: Heads-up — Sales surfaced a batch of legacy accounts on bespoke tiers. They’re being asked to move to the new standardized tiers by the end of the quarter. Need a migration plan + how we treat SLAs/add-ons for them.
Sam: Key ask from customer: keep current effective SLA and burst credits for 12 months. They signed those into contract.
Ivy: Do we have a hard list of which contractual clauses explicitly require grandfathering? I can pull civ docs but need guidance on scope.
Ravi: We should split customers into 3 buckets: 1) short-term renewals (<90d) — negotiate in sales, 2) long-term (>1yr) with negotiated SLA — require legal sign-off, 3) churn-risk where keeping old pricing makes sense.
Jordan: From product POV we need to decide whether to support two runtime behaviors: legacy add-on enforcement vs new tier limits. Supporting both increases complexity and testing burden.
Maya: Proposed conservative approach: allow grandfathered limits + SLAs for contracts with explicit language, but enforce new billing/telemetry. Migration window = 12 months unless customer opts in earlier.
Sam: Sales needs an escalation flow. If customer asks for longer than 12 months, who signs off? Suggest Sales + Legal + RevOps.
Ivy: LegalBot, can you confirm which contract language compels us to keep SLA/add-on terms vs just billing?
LegalBot: quick note: if contract includes "service level" or explicit "priority capacity" clauses we must preserve those terms unless both parties amend. Billing mechanics (skus) can be updated with 30d notice in most NDAs.
Ravi: Ok — implementation note: runtime will expose a "grandfathered_profile_id" on tenant metadata. When present, serving layer applies legacy caps and routing priority. Fallback policy: if capacity constrained, route to compatible variant but preserve SLA routing order.
Jordan: That implies we need per-tenant feature flags + test matrix to cover both paths. Estimate: 2 sprints to add tier mapper + 1 sprint for e2e tests.
Maya: Launch criteria for the migration product work: 1) legal-approved migration policy doc, 2) sales playbook + email templates, 3) runtime flag implemented and QA'd, 4) telemetry events for every migrated request.
Sam: Also add a customer-facing timeline template and checkbox: opt-in earlier, request extension, or accept auto-migration.
Ivy: For telemetry, we need fields: tenant_id, legacy_profile, migration_acceptance_ts, sla_preserved boolean. Add to observability backlog.
Ravi: Can we reuse existing per-route dashboards? If not, will add a per-tenant filter. Impact: minor dashboard refactor.
Jordan: Risk: doubling code paths may increase incident surface. Suggest we gate initial rollout to a pilot of 5 accounts (high-value, varied patterns).
Maya: Pilot sounds right. Sam, propose 5 candidate accounts and ask them to opt into pilot. Provide clear rollback plan (auto-reinstate legacy profile) and escalation path.
Sam: Will do. One more ask: pricing consequences — if the new tier is cheaper, will we issue credits for the transition period?
Ivy: Finance/RevOps to decide. Product should clarify whether we auto-credit or require commercial negotiation.
Maya: Action items: Sam - list pilot accounts by EOD Wed; Legal - produce short decision doc on enforceable clauses; Ravi/Jordan - scoping estimate and pilot rollout plan; Ivy - telemetry schema + RevOps contact.
Sam: On it :thumbsup:
Ravi: I’ll sketch the runtime changes and post a short RFC in #eng-runtime by Friday.
Jordan: I’ll draft the test plan and QA checklist.
Ivy: Looping in RevOps separately.
Maya: Thanks everyone — we’ll sync early next week for signoffs.
